routes.label: Divide total distance by total time

question: An automobile went up a hill at a speed of \(10\) miles an hour and down the same distance at a speed of \(20\) miles an hour. The average speed for the round trip was:
solution:
Average speed is the total distance divided by the total elapsed time. Let each one-way distance be \(d>0\) miles. Using time equal to distance divided by speed, the uphill and downhill times are \(d/10\) and \(d/20\) hours. Thus the total time is
\[
\frac d{10}+\frac d{20}=\frac{3d}{20}.
\]
The total distance is \(2d\), so the average speed is
\[
\frac{2d}{3d/20}=\frac{40}{3}
=13\frac13\text{ mph}.
\]
The positive distance \(d\) cancels, so the result applies to any hill length. The answer is \(\boxed{13\dfrac13\text{ mph}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
